result:
Delivered. Originals byte-identical, kit 45/45 re-verified.

## Item 1 — root is right; both defects reproduced before I changed anything

I reproduced both against my **original exported bytes with my original helpers** first (`probes/probe-root-claims.json`).

The root cause was broader than either defect: my `Closure` **never walked `finding`, `finding-fingerprint` or `execution-plan` objects at all**. Those three domains were exported and never admitted against any schema or order annotation, which is why `evidenceRefs`' `canonical-set` annotation was never enforced. **My original sentence "every record is validated against its owning normative schema" was false as stated**, not merely incomplete. The grammar check tested `in cas` instead of tree membership; the normalizer spec passed only because I'd coincidentally reused identical bytes.

**One measured divergence I report rather than adopt:** root said four graphs have unordered `evidenceRefs`, five refused, "both incomplete Rust disclosure graphs admit". I measure **five unordered and six refused** — `RUN-RS-NO-OWNERSHIP-DISCLOSED` also violates (fact `9369…` before coverage `2d5a…`). Only PARTIAL-ENUMERATION admits. Ordering is decided by the *digest*, since `C` sorts keys — which is why it broke in some graphs and not others.

I closed the class rather than patching three joins: `admit_every_retained_object()` now admits **every** retained typed object through a closed selector map, and an unregistered domain is itself a refusal. Measured: **16 domains, zero uncovered**. Plus finding/execution-plan joins and closure-**tree membership** for grammar members. Six new discriminating negatives (grammar bytes stay in CAS, so each is precisely a membership test). **9 graphs, 2725 checks, 0 failures; 36 negatives all refused** — including the MUST-1 probe now exported as an inspectable graph.

## Item 2 — CB7-SHOULD-1 **retracted in full**

Root is right, and the kit settles it. I imposed `unmetPreconditions[].code == deficiency token`, which no contract states. `perRequirementConsumerBoundary` names the carrier as `EvidenceRequirement.deficiency` and says the boundary "adds no … public detail code"; the imported law distinguishes two outcomes *"because the remedies differ"*; `applicable`'s description is a conjunction, so an empty `unmetPreconditions` is lawful. **16 of 16** outcomes are expressible in the field the law names — my "5 of 16" counted the wrong vocabulary in the wrong field. `REPAIR.EVIDENCE_RUN_UNAVAILABLE` is **not** applicable (it names availability/assurance) and not needed. Demonstrated with two schema+order-admitted descriptors, one imported cause, distinct remedies, zero new codes, plus a collapse control — and expressible ≠ authorized. **No residue requiring source clarification.**

## Items 3 & 4

**MUST-1 stands** — re-measured on the corrected build (394 checks, 0 refusals); the helper fixes touched neither its Coverage, its zero clones facts, nor the dialect refusal. **SHOULD-2 stands** with two of my own wording corrections: reachability is now **129 actually assembled real contexts** (128 admits, 129 refuses) rather than synthetic strings; and root is right that "names no field" was overbroad — the fault *does* name the field, but carries no standalone count, limit or remedy (an earlier heuristic of mine matched `128`/`129` inside hex digests — corrected and disclosed). Bounds re-measured: 128/128/256.

All eight item-4 scope limits are now measurements: only **4 of 33** mutations are strictly single-field; **4 of 6** preimage displays were truncated heads; the D9 comparison was map-vs-enum, like-for-like is **11 → 12**.

Verdict unchanged: **CHANGES_REQUIRED** — one MUST, one SHOULD, one retraction, no new findings.
